:::{#rem-consistent-sequence}
#### Consistency describes a sequence of estimators

An estimator such as the [sample mean](exploratory-descriptive.qmd#def-sample-mean)
is a formula that applies to any sample size,
so $\hparam_1, \hparam_2, \ldots$ is a sequence of estimators,
one for each $n$.
[Unbiasedness](estimation.qmd#def-unbiased) and
[mean squared error](estimation.qmd#def-mse)
describe an estimator at one fixed sample size;
consistency describes what happens to the whole sequence as $n$ grows.
An estimator can be consistent and biased at every $n$,
or unbiased at every $n$ and not consistent
(the single-observation estimator $\Rvar_1$ of a mean is the standard example).
:::
